open.what_it_does: 2.1.218 adds a NEW folder-trust gate in front of registering an agent definition's frontmatter `hooks`. Registration itself (fn SQu@217 / fsd@218, message "Registered ${i} frontmatter hook(s) from ${n} for session ${t}") is unchanged, but both call sites gained a `mvo(e)` trust predicate. `mvo(e)` returns true iff: the agent source is in the trusted set `{plugin, policySettings, built-in, builtin, bundled}` (J0e), OR source is "userSettings"/"flagSettings", OR — for a file-loaded agent — the project the definition folder belongs to has `projects[<key>].hasTrustDialogAccepted === true`. The folder→project key is derived by `psd(baseDir)`: if `basename(baseDir)==="agents"` and `basename(dirname(baseDir))===".claude"`, walk up two levels to the project root, else use baseDir as-is; then `Frn`/`tdr` normalize it and read the global config. On failure the hooks are DROPPED (never registered) and a byte-specific error is logged plus telemetry `tengu_agent_hooks_origin_untrusted` with `{source, surface, fromAdditionalDirectory}`. Applies to BOTH surfaces: subagent spawn (surface "subagent") and the `--agent` main-thread agent (surface "mainThread"). Skill/command frontmatter hooks were deliberately NOT gated (that call site is unchanged in 218). Secondary micro-change: the truthiness test `e.hooks` became `gvo(e.hooks)` (true only if some event bucket has an entry with `hooks.length>0`).

open.what_it_does: 2.1.218 introduces background execution + resume for `context: fork` skills, and with it a deny-rule freezing mechanism so a forked skill's permission scoping survives the fork and the later resume. `ddo(getAppState, allowed, denied, opts)` gains a `frozenCommandDenies` branch: `n?.frozenCommandDenies!==void 0?{...i,alwaysDenyRules:{...i.alwaysDenyRules,command:Mo([...n.frozenCommandDenies,...i.alwaysDenyRules.command??[],...r])}}:qls(i,r)` — i.e. the frozen list is UNIONED ahead of the live deny rules rather than being replaced. `Orn` captures it at fork time: `let u=o?.freezeCommandDenies&&!o?.replaceDenyRules?r.getAppState().toolPermissionContext.alwaysDenyRules.command??[]:void 0` and returns it. `wvo` persists it into an on-disk scoping record validated by a new zod schema `yvo = Pe.object({skillName, attributionName, effort?, frozenCommandDenies: Pe.array(Pe.string().max(1024)).max(1000).optional()})`, alongside a `provenanceMarker` file `{forkedSkill:!0, skillName}`; a write/validate failure aborts the launch (`Fe("subagent_launch","forked_skill_scoping_unpersistable")` / `"forked_skill_scoping_write_failed"`). On resume the record is re-read and re-applied: `let L=D?D.frozenCommandDenies??s.getAppState().toolPermissionContext.alwaysDenyRules.command??[]:void 0, … getAppState:ddo(s.getAppState,x,O,{replaceCommandRules:!0,frozenCommandDenies:L})`, and if the skill no longer resolves to a fork-capable skill the resume is REFUSED: `throw … new sL(\`Agent ${e} ran as forked skill ${D.skillName}, which no longer resolves to a fork-capable skill; refusing to resume it without its permission scoping.\`)`. The point is that `replaceCommandRules:!0` wipes the allow rules for the forked agent, and without frozen denies a resumed background fork would silently come back without the parent session's `alwaysDenyRules.command`.

Note the freeze arm specifically fires when `freezeCommandDenies && !replaceDenyRules`, which is the SkillTool background path (`replaceCommandRules:v, freezeCommandDenies:v`), whereas the user-slash forked path passes `replaceDenyRules:!c`.
